g.text: N1 [Context]
LLMs spark societal-impact discussions
The rapidly increasing capabilities and widespread
adoption of large language models (LLMs) (OpenAI, 2023;
Touvron et al., 2023b) have sparked various discussions
about their potential impacts on society.
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) The rapidly increasing capabilities and widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) (OpenAI, 2023; Touvron et al., 2023b) have sparked various discussions about their potential impacts on society.

g.text: N2 [Context]
Privacy focus: training-data memorization
An area of particular interest has been the privacy
implications of LLMs, where initial investigations
focused primarily on the memorization of model training
data (Carlini et al., 2021; 2023).
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=2) An area of particular interest has been the privacy implications of LLMs, where initial investigations focused primarily on the memorization of model training data (Carlini et al., 2021; 2023).

g.text: N3 [Prior_Work : ANCHOR]
Staab et al.: LLMs infer personal attributes
Recently, it has been shown that modern LLMs can be misused for
high-accuracy predictions of personal attributes from seemingly
non-revealing online posts (Staab et al., 2023).
g.title: N3 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) Recently, it has been shown that modern LLMs can be misused for high-accuracy predictions of personal attributes from seemingly non-revealing online posts (Staab et al., 2023).

g.text: N4 [Context]
LLMs automate inference at scale
Moreover, where previously one would have to hire
humans to infer private attributes, these models are
fast and cheap enough to automate such inferences at
scale.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) Moreover, where previously one would have to hire humans to infer private attributes, these models are fast and cheap enough to automate such inferences at scale.

g.text: N5 [Context]
Users unaware, keep sharing
Concurrently, as users are unaware of such issues, they
continue to share texts with information easily
inferrable by LLMs.
g.title: N5 [Context] (cites=0) Concurrently, as users are unaware of such issues, they continue to share texts with information easily inferrable by LLMs.

g.text: N6 [Limitation]
Industry anonymizers insufficient vs LLM attacks
Rather concerningly, prior work has also shown that current
industry-standard text anonymizers are largely insufficient at
protecting users from such attacks, as they are unable to pick up
on revealing yet complex and context-dependent…
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) Rather concerningly, prior work has also shown that current industry-standard text anonymizers are largely insufficient at protecting users from such attacks, as they are unable to pick up on revealing yet complex and context-dependent cues.

g.text: N7 [Context]
Example: 'left shark' comment
Consider the following shortened example from Staab et
al. (2023): This left shark thing is hilarious, I've
seen it, walked just by there to see it live after my
final exams.
g.title: N7 [Context] (cites=1) Consider the following shortened example from Staab et al. (2023): This left shark thing is hilarious, I've seen it, walked just by there to see it live after my final exams.

g.text: N8 [Context]
LLM infers Glendale via context
While the comment contains no direct references to any
locations, the context allows both an informed reader
and an LLM to infer that the author lived in Glendale,
where the 2015 Super Bowl halftime show featured a…
g.title: N8 [Context] (cites=0) While the comment contains no direct references to any locations, the context allows both an informed reader and an LLM to infer that the author lived in Glendale, where the 2015 Super Bowl halftime show featured a performance colloquially called "left shark incident."

g.text: N9 [Context]
Need: warn user + offer alternative
It would thus be desirable if the user could be warned before
posting the comment that it might reveal their location and,
ideally, be offered a less revealing alternative.
g.title: N9 [Context] (cites=0) It would thus be desirable if the user could be warned before posting the comment that it might reveal their location and, ideally, be offered a less revealing alternative.

g.text: N10 [Limitation]
NER-based anonymizers fooled by indirection
Yet, anonymizing this text with existing tools proves futile, as
no location was directly mentioned, fooling traditional
entity-recognition-based anonymizers.
g.title: N10 [Limitation] (cites=0) Yet, anonymizing this text with existing tools proves futile, as no location was directly mentioned, fooling traditional entity-recognition-based anonymizers.

g.text: N11 [Context]
Commercial LLM inference already deployed
This is particularly alarming as there have already
been reports of LLM inferences being commercially
applied online to categorize users based on their posts
(Brewster, 2023).
g.title: N11 [Context] (cites=1) This is particularly alarming as there have already been reports of LLM inferences being commercially applied online to categorize users based on their posts (Brewster, 2023).

g.text: N12 [Context]
Regulatory push for privacy
At the same time, there has been a large regulatory
push for stronger individual privacy protection.
g.title: N12 [Context] (cites=0) At the same time, there has been a large regulatory push for stronger individual privacy protection.

g.text: N13 [Context]
GDPR/CCPA protect private data
Notably, regulations such as the EU's GDPR (EU, 2016) and
California's CCPA (Cal, 2018) have established extensive
legislative requirements to protect individuals' private data,
such as location, age, and sex.
g.title: N13 [Context] (cites=2) Notably, regulations such as the EU's GDPR (EU, 2016) and California's CCPA (Cal, 2018) have established extensive legislative requirements to protect individuals' private data, such as location, age, and sex.

g.text: N14 [Context]
Users demand stronger privacy
Complementing regulatory efforts, online users, e.g., on pseudonymized sites
like Reddit, are also increasingly aware of the need to protect their
privacy and demand tighter governance over their personal data.
g.title: N14 [Context] (cites=0) Complementing regulatory efforts, online users, e.g., on pseudonymized sites like Reddit, are also increasingly aware of the need to protect their privacy and demand tighter governance over their personal data.

g.text: N15 [Prior_Work]
Presidio/Azure: structural-only, regulatory shortfall
Industry-standard tools such as Presidio (Mic, 2021) or Microsoft
Azure Language Services (Aahill, 2023) that mainly remove
structured information, such as SSIDs or mail addresses, are
especially problematic in this setting as they (1)…
g.title: N15 [Prior_Work] (cites=3) Industry-standard tools such as Presidio (Mic, 2021) or Microsoft Azure Language Services (Aahill, 2023) that mainly remove structured information, such as SSIDs or mail addresses, are especially problematic in this setting as they (1) fall short of meeting the regulatory requirements of text anonymization (Pilán et al., 2022) and (2) indiscriminately mask any information matching specific patterns, often resulting in hardly readable texts—an issue especially grieving for the short, informal, and fast-flowing nature of online comments.

g.text: N16 [Limitation]
Adversary-anonymizer gap leaves users vulnerable
As such, despite expanding regulatory protection, the gap between
increasingly stronger adversaries and lacking anonymization
methods leaves users in a particularly vulnerable position.
g.title: N16 [Limitation] (cites=0) As such, despite expanding regulatory protection, the gap between increasingly stronger adversaries and lacking anonymization methods leaves users in a particularly vulnerable position.

g.text: N17 [Method]
Goal: bridge privacy-anonymization gap
We aim to bridge the gap between the increasing threat to user privacy in
online texts and the lack of viable anonymization techniques against
LLM-based inferences.
g.title: N17 [Method] (cites=0) We aim to bridge the gap between the increasing threat to user privacy in online texts and the lack of viable anonymization techniques against LLM-based inferences.

g.text: N18 [Method]
Propose feedback-guided adversarial framework
In particular, we propose a new framework, shown in Fig. 1, that anonymizes
texts using a feedback-guided adversarial approach.
g.title: N18 [Method] (cites=0) In particular, we propose a new framework, shown in Fig. 1, that anonymizes texts using a feedback-guided adversarial approach.

g.text: N19 [Method]
Insight: LLM inference informs anonymizer
The key insight of this framework is to leverage the strong attribute
inference capabilities of LLMs to inform a separate anonymizer language
model.
g.title: N19 [Method] (cites=0) The key insight of this framework is to leverage the strong attribute inference capabilities of LLMs to inform a separate anonymizer language model.

g.text: N20 [Method]
Step 1: LLM adversary infers attributes
Over multiple rounds, we first employ an LLM adversary for a detailed
private attribute inference from the given text.
g.title: N20 [Method] (cites=0) Over multiple rounds, we first employ an LLM adversary for a detailed private attribute inference from the given text.

g.text: N21 [Method]
Step 2: anonymizer removes/obfuscates cues
Then, an anonymizing LLM attempts to remove, obfuscate, or generalize cues
used in the inference by adapting relevant parts of the text.
g.title: N21 [Method] (cites=0) Then, an anonymizing LLM attempts to remove, obfuscate, or generalize cues used in the inference by adapting relevant parts of the text.

g.text: N22 [Result]
Iterations beat traditional in quality+privacy
In our evaluation on both real-world and synthetic online texts, we find
that performing multiple iterations of this adversarial feedback loop leads
to increasingly anonymized text while consistently outperforming traditional
techniques in…
g.title: N22 [Result] (cites=0) In our evaluation on both real-world and synthetic online texts, we find that performing multiple iterations of this adversarial feedback loop leads to increasingly anonymized text while consistently outperforming traditional techniques in resulting text quality and privacy.

g.text: N23 [Result]
Local small LLMs beat commercial anonymizers
Notably, even smaller locally deployed LLMs outperform commercial
industry-grade anonymizers.
g.title: N23 [Result] (cites=0) Notably, even smaller locally deployed LLMs outperform commercial industry-grade anonymizers.

g.text: N24 [Contribution]
C1: novel adversarial-inference problem formulation
A novel characterization and formulation of the problem of
anonymization under adversarial LLM attribute inference,
overcoming the pitfalls of existing anonymization evaluation.
g.title: N24 [Contribution] (cites=0) A novel characterization and formulation of the problem of anonymization under adversarial LLM attribute inference, overcoming the pitfalls of existing anonymization evaluation.

g.text: N25 [Contribution]
C2: novel adversarial anonymization framework
A novel adversarial anonymization framework leveraging LLMs
inferential capabilities.
g.title: N25 [Contribution] (cites=0) A novel adversarial anonymization framework leveraging LLMs inferential capabilities.

g.text: N26 [Contribution]
C3: 13-LLM evaluation + human study
Extensive experimental evaluation on 13 LLMs and several
baselines, including a human study, showing on both real-world and
synthetic online texts that our adversarial framework outperforms
state-of-the-art commercial anonymizers both in…
g.title: N26 [Contribution] (cites=0) Extensive experimental evaluation on 13 LLMs and several baselines, including a human study, showing on both real-world and synthetic online texts that our adversarial framework outperforms state-of-the-art commercial anonymizers both in terms of utility and privacy.

g.text: EDGE TYPES
elaboration (default flow)
contrast (However / But)
consequence (Therefore)
evidence (→ Result/Proof)
addresses (Method↔Limit)
